entries.title: White Collar Boxing FAQ | Training, Sparring & Fight Camps
entries.content: Skip to main content GYM: Anchor Hall, Bulwer Rd, Barnet, London EN5 5EX (Northern Line) Gary Foley: 07749 116927 · Sean Murphy: 07729 980677 WHITE COLLAR BOXING LONDON · EST. 20+ YEARS Menu Change colour theme Dark Frequently Asked Questions White Collar Boxing Training FAQ Clear answers on how white collar boxing works, what to expect at your first Barnet gym session, and how we prepare you safely for the ring. Training & Eligibility What is white collar boxing? White collar boxing originated in the late 1980s as a structured way for men and women in professional and executive roles to train like competitive boxers and participate in regulated bouts, typically raising money for charity. Bouts usually consist of three two-minute rounds using 16oz gloves and protective headgear. Do I need any prior boxing experience to join? No. Our Basic / Beginner Boxing Training tier is specifically designed for complete novices. We teach stance, balance, footwork, guard position, and punch mechanics from scratch before introducing advanced combinations. Do I have to compete in a fight night to train with you? Not at all. More than half of our members train strictly for cardiovascular conditioning, strength, stress relief, and skill development without ever stepping into a competitive bout. Safety, Sparring & Equipment Is sparring mandatory? Sparring is never forced on beginners. You only progress to controlled, supervised technical sparring once your defence, conditioning, and composure have been signed off by Gary Foley or Sean Murphy. What equipment do I need for my first session? For your first introductory session, comfortable sportswear, indoor trainers, a towel, and water are sufficient. Once you train regularly, we recommend your own 180-inch hand wraps, 16oz training gloves, and a custom-fitted gumshield. Location, Trainers & Bookings Who are the trainers at White Collar Boxing Training? Sessions are led by Gary Foley (20+ years of London white collar boxing experience and 9+ years as a qualified trainer) and Sean Murphy (Commonwealth Games Gold Medallist, British Lonsdale Belt Outright winner, and World Title contender). Where does training take place? All sessions take place at Anchor Hall, Bulwer Rd, Barnet, London EN5 5EX (coordinates 51.651161, -0.17987), close to High Barnet Underground station and New Barnet National Rail station. How do I book a 1-to-1 session or join a class? Call Head Coach Gary Foley directly on 07749 116927 or Senior Coach Sean Murphy on 07729 980677, or visit our Get in Touch page.

entries.title: Our Story | History of White Collar Boxing in London & NYC
entries.content: Skip to main content GYM: Anchor Hall, Bulwer Rd, Barnet, London EN5 5EX (Northern Line) Gary Foley: 07749 116927 · Sean Murphy: 07729 980677 WHITE COLLAR BOXING LONDON · EST. 20+ YEARS Menu Change colour theme Dark From Gleason's Gym (1988) to Anchor Hall, London The Story & Heritage of White Collar Boxing How corporate professionals in New York and London transformed three-round executive bouts into an international combat sport and charity fundraising movement. From Gleason's Gym in Brooklyn to London's Executive Rings White collar boxing is a form of boxing in which men and women in white-collar professions train to fight at special events. Most have had no prior boxing experience before stepping onto the gym floor. 1988: The Birth of White Collar Boxing in New York The movement began at the legendary Gleason's Gym in New York City in 1988, when gym owner Bruce Silverglade paired two recreational executive members — Richard Novak, an attorney, and Joelarden / fellow PhD and corporate professionals — for a supervised, three-round exhibition bout. What started as a monthly Friday-night tradition for Wall Street bankers, doctors, lawyers, and media executives rapidly evolved into an international phenomenon. The Rise of London Executive & Charity Fight Nights By the early 2000s, white collar boxing had established a permanent home in London and across the United Kingdom. In the City of London, Canary Wharf, and North London, professionals discovered that preparing for a three-round boxing match delivered a physical and psychological transformation that no ordinary health club or treadmill could replicate. At the same time, charity gala fight nights transformed white collar bouts into prestigious black-tie fundraising evenings, raising millions of pounds for UK charities while giving everyday professionals the unforgettable experience of walking out to their chosen entrance track under arena lights. Safety, Governance & The International White Collar Boxing Association As the sport grew globally, formal safety and matchmaking standards became essential. Aligned with the International White Collar Boxing Association (IWCBA) and modern UK amateur/white-collar safety protocols, legitimate white collar boxing enforces: Fair Matchmaking: Opponents are paired strictly by weight class, age bracket, fitness baseline, and total hours of ring experience. Protective Equipment: Mandatory 16oz competition gloves, fitted headguards, gumshields, and groin protectors. Medical Oversight: Pre-bout medical screening and ringside doctors/paramedics at every sanctioned show. 3 × 2-Minute Rounds: High-tempo, controlled round durations with a standing eight-count and safety-first refereeing. Our Mission at Anchor Hall, Barnet (EN5 5EX) Founded on over 20 years of London white collar boxing experience, our gym at Anchor Hall, Bulwer Rd, Barnet, London EN5 5EX brings together Head Coach Gary Foley and Commonwealth Games Gold Medallist & Outright British Lonsdale Belt winner Sean Murphy. We exist to ensure that every executive, founder, and newcomer who steps through the ropes does so with authentic British boxing technique, supreme conditioning, and unshakeable self-belief. Ready to write your own chapter? Explore what's involved in our 3-tier fight camps or book your 1-to-1 assessment today.

entries.title: What's Involved | Basic, Amateur & Advanced Fight Camps
entries.content: Skip to main content GYM: Anchor Hall, Bulwer Rd, Barnet, London EN5 5EX (Northern Line) Gary Foley: 07749 116927 · Sean Murphy: 07729 980677 WHITE COLLAR BOXING LONDON · EST. 20+ YEARS Menu Change colour theme Dark Three Progressive Skill Tiers · IWCBA Safety Aligned What's Involved in Your White Collar Boxing Camp From non-contact beginner padwork and heavy-bag conditioning to 12-week executive charity fight camps with full ringside cornering. Three Progressive Tiers of White Collar Boxing Coaching Every contender who walks through the doors at Anchor Hall, Barnet (EN5 5EX) brings a different athletic background, schedule, and goal. Whether you are training purely for executive stress relief and peak cardiovascular fitness or preparing for an 8-to-12-week charity bout in front of 500 guests, our curriculum is structured into three progressive tiers. Tier 1: Basic / Beginner Boxing Training (The Novice) Designed for complete newcomers with zero prior boxing or combat sports experience. Technical Focus: Balanced orthodox and southpaw stance, guard discipline, distance management, footwork pivots, and crisp straight punches (jab and cross) plus foundational hooks. Conditioning: Boxing-specific skipping, shadow-boxing rounds, heavy-bag combinations, and core stability circuits. Contact Policy: 100% non-contact. You work exclusively on the focus mitts with Gary Foley or Sean Murphy and on the leather heavy bags. Tier 2: Amateur / Mid-Level Boxing Training (The Contender) Built for intermediate boxers and professionals preparing for their first regulated white collar or charity boxing match. Technical Focus: Multi-punch combinations (3 to 5 punch sequences), defensive head movement (slips, rolls, pull-counters), parrying, and ring cutting. Conditioning: High-intensity 2-minute and 3-minute interval rounds engineered to replicate the anaerobic demands of a 3 × 2-minute white collar bout. Contact Policy: Optional, closely refereed technical drills and progressive sparring in full protective equipment (16oz sparring gloves, cheek-protector headguard, custom gumshield, and groin guard). Tier 3: Advanced Competitive Fight Camp (The Main Event) Tailored for experienced white collar boxers and returning contenders targeting high-profile London gala shows. Technical Focus: Advanced counter-punching, rhythm manipulation, inside fighting, southpaw/orthodox tactical adjustments, and opponent-specific game plans. Conditioning: 8-to-12-week periodised fight camp covering strength, explosive power, weight management, and 8-to-10 championship rounds per session. Fight Night Support: Full dressing-room hand wrapping, warm-up pad work, and experienced ringside cornering from Gary Foley and Sean Murphy. Tier Comparison Matrix Training Dimension Tier 01: Basic / Beginner Tier 02: Amateur / Mid-Level Tier 03: Advanced Fight Camp Prior Experience Required None (Complete Beginners) 4+ weeks foundational boxing Previous bout or advanced camp Round Structure 6 × 2-minute technical rounds 8 × 2-minute high-pace rounds 10 × 3-minute championship rounds 1-to-1 Pad Work Foundational mechanics & defence Combination flow & counter-punching Tactical fight-night simulation Sparring & Contact Non-contact (Pads & Heavy Bags) Controlled technical sparring (16oz) Full refereed fight-camp sparring Target Outcome Executive fitness, fat loss & skill First charity / white collar bout Main-event white collar competition Mandatory Equipment & Safety Governance We adhere strictly to International White Collar Boxing Association (IWCBA) safety principles: Hand Protection: Every boxer must wear 4.5-metre cotton hand wraps under properly weighted leather gloves (14oz to 16oz for bag and pad work; strictly 16oz for any sparring). Protective Gear for Sparring: Fitted boil-and-bite or custom dentist gumshield, padded headguard, and groin protector are mandatory before stepping through the ropes for contact drills.
